page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is an Arm-based cloud instance powered by the 64-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. Designed with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation, each of the 64 vCPUs runs a single dedicated thread without simultaneous multithreading. The processor incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 80 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 512 GB of RAM at an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth. In multi-threaded workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core (26,681.0), PassMark physics testing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 717.79 GB/sec. Memory operations show extreme bandwidth, hitting 7,912.04 GB/sec in cached 16 KB read tests and 350.71 GB/sec in 256 MB uncached reads. Application-level evaluations reflect this architectural strength with 134.03 million Redis SET operations per second, high static web serving throughput, and superior Clang compilation performance.

The hardware configuration does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, meaning persistent storage must be provisioned over network block storage. While single-threaded computational tasks and text processing perform in the average range, the dense dedicated 64-core Arm layout delivers strong performance-per-watt and cost-effective scaling for parallel architectures.

Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is well suited for high-density in-memory databases like Redis or Memcached, large-scale software compilation, batch processing, static web traffic handling, and enterprise analytics that benefit from high memory-to-vCPU ratios without requiring hardware acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is a high-memory compute instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture at 3.0 GHz. With one thread per core and no hyperthreading, the instance provides 512 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an 80 MB L3 cache. It contains no integrated GPU acceleration or local disk storage, relying on network-attached volumes. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution, Clang compilation, and cached memory bandwidth exceeding 7,900 GB/sec, while maintaining over 134 million Redis operations per second. Delivering balanced qualitative resource efficiency through energy-conscious Arm silicon, the c4a-highmem-64 is designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, in-memory key-value databases, distributed caching layers, high-concurrency web serving, and parallel software build pipelines.
